question: Consider DSB-SC amplitude modulation with signal s(t) = m(t)*cos(omega_c*t), where M(j*omega) is the Fourier transform of m(t). Compute the Fourier transform S(j*omega) of s(t) in terms of M.

steps.description: Start with the definition of the modulated signal s(t)
Express cosine in terms of complex exponentials

steps.notes: Correct distribution of m(t) into both terms.
FT is linear; sum of transforms equals transform of sum.

steps.description: Factor out the constant 1/2 from each term
Use the frequency shift property of Fourier transform: Fourier transform of m(t)*exp(I*omega_0*t) is M(j*(omega - omega_0))
steps.notes: Frequency shift: FT{m(t)exp(Iω₀t)} = M(I(ω−ω₀)); first term ω₀=+ω_c, second term ω₀=−ω_c. Both applied correctly.
